newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab and Jewish lawmakers no match for bulldozer.
newsitem.headline: Arab and Jewish lawmakers no match for bulldozer.

text.p: A handful of Arab and Jewish members of Israel's parliament was no match for bulldozers that broke ground on Tuesday for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We have come to try to stop the work on what is a very dangerous move for all those who are interested in peace," said legislator Tamar Gojanzki of the leftist Democratic Front for Peace and Equality, who took part in the token protest.
Bulldozers easily manouevered around her and other lawmakers who were allowed past an Israeli army cordon around Jabal Abu Ghneim, where Israel plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews.
Hundreds of troops in battle gear ringed the construction site on a windswept hill to keep Palestinian protesters away as heavy shovels pierced the earth on the first day of work.
Soldiers scuffled with Israeli Arab students trying to reach a Palestinian protest camp on an adjacent hill, hitting them with rifle butts.
The digging plunged Israelis and Palestinians deeper into a crisis brewing since Israel approved construction of the new settlement that the PLO says violates bilateral peace agreements.
Israel put police and the army on high alert to pre-empt violence.

"I have long worked for peace and never despaired. But today I am beginning to despair," said PLO official Faisal al-Husseini, who pitched two tents on Monday opposite the settlement site that Israel calls Har Homa.
He said the Israeli move left Palestinians with only one option -- "to go down to the streets".
Husseini and about 15 other Palestinians and Israelis waited in pouring rain early on Tuesday for the construction to begin.

When skies cleared at about 2:40 p.m. (1240 GMT) three bulldozers rolled off flatbed trucks travelling in heavily guarded convoys and begin shoveling dirt along what will be a main road in the new settlement. Surveyors set up tripods and took measurements.
The settlement will be another link in a concrete chain of apartment blocks that Israel has built to cement its hold on East Jerusalem and separate it from the rest of the West Bank.
Israel regards all of Jerusalem as its "eternal capital". The PLO wants East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of a Palestinian state.
